  >>      1: 7 Medications to Avoid During the First Trimester of Pregnancy Pregnancy changes the way you think about everything. Suddenly, even the smallest decisions feel important. You get a headache and stop before taking anything. You catch a cold and wonder if normal medications are still safe. You open your medicine cabinet and realize something frightening… The medications you trusted before pregnancy may not always be safe now. And the reason becomes especially important during the first trimester. This is the stage where your baby’s organs are forming. The brain begins developing. The heart starts beating. The spinal cord, limbs, kidneys, and facial structures are all taking shape. It’s one of the most delicate periods of human development, which means certain medications can interfere with these processes in ways many women never expect. What makes this even more concerning is that some risky medications are very common. Some are prescription drugs. Others are medications people buy casually over the counter without thinking twice. In this video, we’re going to walk through 7 medications that should generally be avoided during the first trimester of pregnancy, explaining not only what these medications are, but exactly why they may be harmful and what safer options may exist. Because when you understand what’s happening inside your body during pregnancy, protecting your baby becomes much less confusing — and far less frightening. Now Why Medication Safety Matters in the First Trimester The first trimester is often called the foundation stage of pregnancy because this is when organogenesis occurs — the process where your baby’s major organs and body systems begin forming. During these early weeks, cells are dividing rapidly and transforming into specialized tissues. The brain, spinal cord, heart, kidneys, limbs, and facial structures all begin developing during this period. Because development happens so quickly, the embryo is extremely sensitive to outside influences, including medications. Certain drugs are able to cross the placenta and enter the developing fetal circulation. Once there, they may interfere with cell signaling, tissue growth, blood flow, or organ formation. Some medications can increase the risk of miscarriage, while others may contribute to structural birth defects or developmental complications. Research published by organizations like the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention emphasizes the importance of medication review before and during pregnancy. This does not mean every medication is dangerous. Many medications are necessary and lifesaving during pregnancy. The goal is not fear — it’s awareness, caution, and informed decision-making. The first medication is Isotretinoin (Severe Acne Medication) One of the most dangerous medications during pregnancy is Isotretinoin, a powerful drug commonly prescribed for severe cystic acne. This medication is extremely effective at reducing oil production and controlling severe acne outbreaks. However, it is also one of the most well-known teratogenic medications in medicine, meaning it can cause severe birth defects if taken during pregnancy. The reason isotretinoin is so dangerous is because it directly affects how cells grow, divide, and mature. During the first trimester, your baby’s organs are developing rapidly, and isotretinoin can disrupt these developmental pathways. Studies published in the New England Journal of Medicine have shown strong associations between isotretinoin exposure and abnormalities involving the brain, skull, ears, eyes, heart, and facial structures. Some infants exposed during pregnancy develop central nervous system abnormalities or congenital heart defects. There is also a significantly increased risk of miscarriage and premature delivery. Because the risks are so serious, strict pregnancy prevention programs exist for women taking isotretinoin. In many countries, women are required to undergo regular pregnancy testing and use contraception before receiving prescriptions. What makes this medication particularly important to discuss is that many pregnancies are unplanned. A woman may continue taking the medication before realizing she is pregnant. This is why dermatologists strongly advise stopping isotretinoin before conception and discussing safer acne alternatives during pregnancy. Treatments like topical azelaic acid or certain pregnancy-safe skincare approaches may be considered instead under medical supervision. Number 2: Ibuprofen and NSAIDs Many people are surprised to learn that common painkillers like Ibuprofen may not be ideal during early pregnancy. Ibuprofen belongs to a class of medications known as NSAIDs, or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. These medications reduce inflammation and relieve pain by blocking substances called prostaglandins. While that sounds harmless, prostaglandins play important roles in implantation, blood flow regulation, and pregnancy maintenance. Several studies published in journals such as BMJ have suggested that frequent NSAID use during early pregnancy may be associated with an increased risk of miscarriage. Researchers believe this may occur because prostaglandin suppression can interfere with implantation and early placental development. Later in pregnancy, the risks become even more concerning. NSAIDs can affect fetal circulation and may prematurely close a vital fetal blood vessel called the ductus arteriosus. Because of this, these medications are especially avoided during the third trimester. Another issue is that many people use ibuprofen casually for headaches, muscle pain, fever, or menstrual-like cramping before realizing they are pregnant. Healthcare providers often recommend Acetaminophen as a safer alternative for pain and fever during pregnancy when used appropriately. However, even safer medications should still be used thoughtfully and according to medical guidance. The important lesson here is that “over-the-counter” does not automatically mean “safe during pregnancy.” Number 3: Warfarin (Blood Thinner) Warfarin is a medication used to prevent dangerous blood clots, strokes, and certain heart complications. For many patients, it can be lifesaving. But during pregnancy — especially the first trimester — it carries serious risks to the developing baby. Warfarin crosses the placenta easily and can interfere with fetal development during critical stages of organ formation. One of the most recognized complications is something called fetal warfarin syndrome. This condition may include abnormal facial development, nasal deformities, skeletal abnormalities, growth restriction, and developmental complications. Studies published in journals like Circulation have documented these risks extensively, particularly when exposure occurs between weeks 6 and 12 of pregnancy. The medication works by blocking vitamin K–dependent clotting factors. Unfortunately, vitamin K is also involved in developmental pathways related to bone and cartilage formation in the fetus. In addition to structural abnormalities, warfarin exposure may increase the risk of miscarriage, bleeding complications, and neurological problems. For pregnant women who require anticoagulation therapy, safer alternatives such as heparin are often used because they do not cross the placenta significantly. What makes this topic important is that many women taking blood thinners may become pregnant unexpectedly. That’s why pre-pregnancy medication counseling is extremely important for women with clotting disorders or heart conditions. Pregnancy does not mean stopping all medications blindly. It means adjusting treatment carefully to protect both mother and baby safely. Number 4: ACE Inhibitors (Blood Pressure Medications) Medications such as Lisinopril and other ACE inhibitors are commonly prescribed for high blood pressure, kidney disease, and heart conditions. Outside of pregnancy, they are highly effective medications. But during pregnancy, they can become dangerous to fetal development. These medications work by blocking the renin-angiotensin system, which helps regulate blood pressure and fluid balance. However, this same system is also critical for fetal kidney development. Research published in journals like The Lancet and The New England Journal of Medicine has shown that ACE inhibitor exposure during pregnancy can interfere with normal kidney formation in the fetus. This may lead to reduced amniotic fluid levels, poor lung development, impaired skull growth, and fetal growth restriction. Reduced amniotic fluid is especially concerning because amniotic fluid protects the baby and supports normal organ development. When fluid levels become too low, complications can become severe. Although the greatest risks are often associated with second and third trimester exposure, many experts recommend avoiding ACE inhibitors entirely during pregnancy because early developmental effects may still occur. Safer blood pressure medications are available during pregnancy, including options such as labetalol and methyldopa under physician supervision. Women with chronic hypertension who are planning pregnancy are usually advised to review their medications beforehand to reduce risk during those crucial first weeks of development. Number 5: Tetracycline Antibiotics Tetracycline antibiotics are commonly used to treat infections such as acne, respiratory infections, and certain bacterial illnesses. While effective, they are generally avoided during pregnancy because of how they interact with developing bones and teeth. Tetracyclines bind strongly to calcium. During pregnancy, calcium plays a critical role in fetal bone and tooth formation. When tetracycline crosses the placenta, it can accumulate in fetal tissues undergoing calcification. Research published in The Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy has shown that exposure may lead to permanent tooth discoloration and impaired bone growth in the developing baby. Teeth affected by tetracycline exposure may later appear yellow, gray, or brown. Another concern is that these medications may interfere with normal skeletal development during critical growth periods. Although the risks are more pronounced later in pregnancy when teeth and bones mineralize more actively, many clinicians avoid tetracyclines throughout pregnancy to minimize potential complications. Fortunately, many infections during pregnancy can be treated with safer alternatives such as penicillin-based antibiotics or cephalosporins, depending on the infection involved. This is why self-medicating leftover antibiotics during pregnancy can be risky. Not every antibiotic is interchangeable, and pregnancy changes the safety profile of many medications. Number 6: High-Dose Vitamin A Supplements Many people assume vitamins are always safe during pregnancy. But with vitamin A, excessive amounts can actually become harmful. Vitamin A is essential for vision, immune function, and fetal development. However, high-dose vitamin A supplements — especially synthetic retinoid forms — can increase the risk of birth defects during the first trimester. Research published in teratology and developmental biology journals has linked excessive vitamin A intake to abnormalities involving the brain, skull, heart, and facial structures. The reason is that retinoids strongly influence gene expression and embryonic cell differentiation. During early fetal development, small disruptions in these signaling pathways can lead to structural abnormalities. This is why prenatal vitamins contain carefully controlled amounts of vitamin A rather than extremely high doses. Some people unintentionally consume excess vitamin A through multiple supplements or certain acne products derived from retinoids. Liver-based supplements can also contain very high concentrations. Healthcare providers usually recommend avoiding unnecessary high-dose supplementation during pregnancy unless specifically prescribed. The important point here is balance. Vitamin A deficiency is harmful, but excessive intake can also be dangerous. Pregnancy requires careful nutritional moderation rather than assuming more is always better. Lastly, Misoprostol Misoprostol is a medication with several medical uses, including ulcer prevention, labor induction, and medical pregnancy termination. Because it stimulates strong uterine contractions, it can be dangerous during early pregnancy if used unintentionally or without medical supervision. Misoprostol works by acting on prostaglandin receptors in the uterus, causing the uterine muscles to contract. During the first trimester, this can lead to miscarriage, heavy bleeding, or incomplete pregnancy loss. In pregnancies that continue after exposure, studies and case reports have documented associations with certain congenital abnormalities, including limb defects and neurological complications. The World Health Organization recognizes misoprostol as an important medication in obstetric care, but emphasizes that its use must occur under proper medical supervision because timing, dosage, and indication matter significantly. One reason this medication is important to discuss is because in some regions, people may obtain it without full understanding of how powerful it is physiologically. Pregnancy is extremely sensitive during the first trimester, and medications capable of altering uterine activity should never be used casually. Even medications with legitimate medical uses can become dangerous when taken inappropriately during pregnancy. In conclusion, the first trimester is one of the most delicate stages of pregnancy, but it’s also one of the most important times to become informed about what enters your body. And here’s the reassuring truth… You do not need to live in fear of every medication. You simply need awareness, caution, and guidance. Always speak with your healthcare provider before starting, stopping, or continuing medications during pregnancy — including over-the-counter drugs, supplements, and herbal remedies. Because protecting your baby doesn’t come from panic… It comes from informed decisions made with knowledge and care. Thanks for sticking with me till the end!   >>      1: Cash Flow Problems: Why Small Businesses Run Out of Money Even When Sales Are Growing One of the biggest reasons small businesses fail is not because they lack customers, and not because their products are bad. Understanding how cash flow works is therefore essential for any company that wants long-term survival and sustainable growth. Cash flow refers to the movement of money into and out of a business. Positive cash flow means more money is entering the business than leaving it. Negative cash flow means expenses and outgoing payments are larger than incoming revenue during a certain period. Even businesses with strong monthly sales can experience severe negative cash flow if they do not manage timing properly. One common cause of cash flow problems is delayed customer payments. Many businesses operate using invoices instead of immediate payment systems. A company may complete a large project worth thousands of dollars, but the client may not pay for thirty, sixty, or even ninety days. During that waiting period, the business still has to continue operating. Employee salaries must still be paid. Office rent remains due. Inventory may need replenishment. Many financially stable businesses maintain reserve funds specifically for unexpected disruptions. Businesses without reserves may struggle to survive even temporary disruptions. Customer concentration risk is another major issue. Some businesses depend heavily on one or two major clients for most of their revenue. While large clients may generate strong income, losing a major contract can severely damage cash flow stability. Diversifying revenue sources reduces dependency risk and improves long-term resilience. Operational efficiency also influences financial performance.          67: Amazon 
  >>     68: A humidifier may not top your baby registry , but it can be a real comfort during dry winter months — especially when sniffles strike. As a mom of four, I’ve learned to keep mine close ’s amazing how much easier everyone sleeps (and breathes!) with a little extra humidity in the air. The best baby humidifiers quietly add moisture to help ease congestion and keep sensitive skin from drying out, sans noisy gurgles or steamy surprises. “Ideally, a baby’s room should have 30 to 50% humidity,” says Dyan Hes, M.D ., a pediatrician at Northwell Lenox Hill Hospital. If the air feels desert-dry, a humidifier can help bring it back to that comfy sweet spot.  Of course, there are plenty of factors to consider before buying a humidifier. You'll want to think about the type, ease of cleaning, and coverage area, for starters. And if it happens to look good in baby’s space, too, even better! Here’s how I picked the best baby humidifiers — with expert insight and parent feedback from What to Expect's community leading the way. How I Chose the Best Baby Humidifiers
         69: To make sure these picks were both safe and practical, I not only spoke with Dr. Hes, but several other pediatricians and sleep experts as well, including:  Emily Wisniewski, M.D. , a pediatrician with Mercy Family Care Physicians in Baltimore, Maryland Lauren Levine, M.D. , a pediatrician affiliated with NewYork-Presbyterian/Columbia University Irving Medical Center and NewYork-Presbyterian Morgan Stanley Children's Hospital Ellen M. Schumann, M.D. , a clerkship director at the Medical College of Wisconsin Luis E. Ortiz, M.D. , a physician in the Sleep Center at Johns Hopkins All Children’s Hospital Melanie Sue Collins, M.D. , medical director of the Division of Pediatric Pulmonary and Sleep Medicine at Connecticut Children's Medical Center Punita Ponda, M.D. , a New York-based Northwell Health physician who specializes in allergy and immunology and pediatrics Based on their guidance, in addition to feedback from parents in the What to Expect community, I ensured all of our selections met the following criteria: Cool mist : The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) recommends using a cool mist humidifier over a warm mist one, as the latter could lead to accidental burns if knocked over. These are preferred “We get worried if there is warmth—this can be an environment that allows mold and other infectious bugs to grow,” she explains.  Easy to clean : “It is important to clean and dry the tank and any parts that come in contact with water," says Dr. Levine. "Some tanks are designed to make this easier, others make it nearly impossible." Dr. Hes recommends changing the water and wiping the unit down daily, giving it a “good scrubbing with a brush” every week. (You can use vinegar and a toothbrush to get into any small crevices.) “This will ensure you clean out any mold or bacteria hiding in the humidifier,” Dr. Hes says.  Automatic shut-off : “Since you usually run a humidifier at night while your baby is sleeping, you also should look for a machine with an automatic shut-off so that if the tank runs out of water it will turn off,” says Dr. Levine. Appropriate coverage : Too small and there will be no benefit; too big and you risk mold growth. Look at the model's recommended square footage when shopping to ensure it's compatible with the room you're planning to keep it in. Directional flow : While not always necessary, having the option to point the mist where you want it to go is always a perk, says Dr. Schumann.

href=\"/wiki/Referral_marketing\" title=\"Referral marketing\">Referral marketing</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"/wiki/Content_marketing\" title=\"Content marketing\">Content marketing</a></li>\n<li><a title=\"Mobile advertising\">Mobile advertising</a></li></ul></td>\n</tr><tr><th class=\"sidebar-heading\" style=\"background:#ddddff;\">\n<a href=\"/wiki/Affiliate_marketing\" title=\"Affiliate marketing\">Affiliate marketing</a></th></tr><tr><td class=\"sidebar-content\">\n<ul><li><a href=\"/wiki/Cost_per_action\" title=\"Cost per action\">Cost per action</a></li>\n<li><a class=\"sidebar-content\">\n<ul><li><a href=\"/wiki/Keyword_density\" title=\"Keyword density\">Keyword density</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"/wiki/Keyword_research\" title=\"Keyword research\">Keyword research</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"/wiki/PageRank\" title=\"PageRank\">PageRank</a></li>\n<li><a href=\"/wiki/WordPress\" title=\"WordPress\">WordPress CMS</a></li></ul></td>\n</tr><tr><td class=\"sidebar-navbar\"><link rel=\"mw-deduplicated-inline-style\" href=\"mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1333133064\" /><style data-mw-deduplicate=\"TemplateStyles:r1239400231\">.mw-parser-output .navbar{display:inline;font-size:88%;font-weight:normal}.mw-parser-output .navbar-collapse{float:left;text-align:left}.mw-parser-output .navbar-boxtext{word-spacing:0}.mw-parser-output .navbar ul{display:inline-block;white-space:nowrap;line-height:inherit}.mw-parser-output .navbar-brackets::before{margin-right:-0.125em;content:\"[ \"}.mw-parser-output .navbar-brackets::after{margin-left:-0.125em;content:\" ]\"}.mw-parser-output .navbar li{word-spacing:-0.125em}.mw-parser-output .navbar a>span,.mw-parser-output .navbar a>abbr{text-decoration:inherit}.mw-parser-output .navbar-mini abbr{font-variant:small-caps;border-bottom:none;text-decoration:none;cursor:inherit}.mw-parser-output .navbar-ct-full{font-size:114%;margin:0 7em}.mw-parser-output .navbar-ct-mini{font-size:114%;margin:0 4em}html.skin-theme-clientpref-night .mw-parser-output .navbar li a abbr{color:var(--color-base)!important}@media(prefers-color-scheme:dark){html.skin-theme-clientpref-os .mw-parser-output .navbar li a abbr{color:var(--color-base)!important}}@media print{.mw-parser-output .navbar{display:none!important}}</style><div class=\"navbar plainlinks hlist navbar-mini\"><ul><li class=\"nv-view\"><a href=\"/wiki/Template:Internet_marketing\" title=\"Template:Internet marketing\"><abbr title=\"View this template\">v</abbr></a></li><li class=\"nv-talk\"><a href=\"/wiki/Template_talk:Internet_marketing\" title=\"Template talk:Internet marketing\"><abbr title=\"Discuss this template\">t</abbr></a></li><li class=\"nv-edit\"><a href=\"/wiki/Special:EditPage/Template:Internet_marketing\" title=\"Special:EditPage/Template:Internet marketing\"><abbr title=\"Edit this template\">e</abbr></a></li></ul></div></td></tr></tbody></table>\n<p><b>Search engine optimization</b> (<b>SEO</b>) is the practice of improving the visibility and overall performance of websites and web pages in <a href=\"/wiki/Search_engine_results_pages\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Search engine results pages\">search engine results pages</a> (SERPs).<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;1-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-:1-1\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>1<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> It focuses on increasing the quantity and quality of traffic from unpaid (organic) search results rather than paid advertising.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-googlesitemaps&#95;2-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-googlesitemaps-2\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>2<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> SEO applies to multiple search formats, including web, image, video, news, academic, and vertical search engines, as well as AI-assisted search interfaces.\n</p><p>SEO is commonly used as part of a broader digital marketing strategy and involves optimizing technical infrastructure, content relevance, and authority signals to improve rankings for user queries.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-infoseeknyt&#95;3-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-infoseeknyt-3\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>3<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> The objective of SEO is to attract users who are actively searching for information, products, or services, thereby improving brand visibility, user engagement, and conversions.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-ms-wmguide&#95;4-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-ms-wmguide-4\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>4<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<meta property=\"mw:PageProp/toc\" />\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading2\"><h2 id=\"History\">History</h2></div>\n<p><a href=\"/wiki/Webmaster\" title=\"Webmaster\">Webmasters</a> and content providers began optimizing websites for search engines in the mid-1990s as the first search engines were cataloging the early <a href=\"/wiki/World_Wide_Web\" title=\"World Wide Web\">Web</a>. Search engine users would query the <a href=\"/wiki/Uniform_Resource_Locator\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Uniform Resource Locator\">URL</a> of a page, and then receive information found on the page, if it existed in the search engine's <a href=\"/wiki/Search_engine_indexing\" title=\"Search engine indexing\">index</a>.\n</p><p><a href=\"/wiki/Aliweb\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Aliweb\">ALIWEB</a> and the earliest versions of search engines required website developers to manually upload website index files in order to be searchable and widely did not utilize any form of ranking algorithm for user queries.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-:1&#95;1-1\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-:1-1\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>1<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> The emergence of automated <a href=\"/wiki/Web_crawler\" title=\"Web crawler\">web crawlers</a> would later be used to proactively discover and index websites. This led to website developers to optimize their website\u2019s search signals, including the use of <a href=\"/wiki/Meta_tag\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Meta tag\">meta tags</a>, to achieve greater visibility in search results.\n</p><p>According to a 2004 article by former industry analyst and current <a href=\"/wiki/Google\" title=\"Google\">Google</a> employee <a href=\"/wiki/Danny_Sullivan_(technologist)\" title=\"Danny Sullivan (technologist)\">Danny Sullivan</a>, the phrase \"search engine optimization\" came into use in 1997. Sullivan credits SEO practitioner Bruce Clay as one of the first people to popularize the term.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-5\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-5\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>5<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p><p>In some cases, early <a href=\"/wiki/Search_algorithm\" title=\"Search algorithm\">search algorithms</a> weighted particular <a href=\"/wiki/HTML_attribute\" title=\"HTML attribute\">HTML attributes</a> in ways that could be leveraged by web content providers to manipulate their search rankings.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-6\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-6\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>6<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> As early as 1997, search engine providers began adjusting their algorithms to prevent these actions.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-infoseeknyt&#95;3-1\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-infoseeknyt-3\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>3<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> Eventually, search engines would incorporate more meaningful measures of page purpose, including the more recent development of semantic search.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-7\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-7\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>7<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Some search engines frequently sponsor SEO conferences, webchats, and seminars. Major search engines provide information and guidelines to help with website optimization.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-g-wmguide&#95;8-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-g-wmguide-8\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>8<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-ms-wmguide&#95;4-1\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-ms-wmguide-4\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>4<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> Google has a <a href=\"/wiki/Sitemaps\" title=\"Sitemaps\">Sitemaps</a> program to help webmasters learn if Google is having any problems indexing their website and also provides data on Google traffic to the website.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-googlesitemaps&#95;2-1\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-googlesitemaps-2\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>2<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> <a href=\"/wiki/Bing_Webmaster_Center\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Bing Webmaster Center\">Bing Webmaster Tools</a> provides a way for webmasters to submit a sitemap and web feeds, allows users to determine the \"crawl rate\", and track the web pages index status.\n</p><p>In 2015, it was reported that <a href=\"/wiki/Google\" title=\"Google\">Google</a> was developing and promoting mobile search as a key feature within future products, resulting in brands and marketers shifting toward mobile-first experiences.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-9\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-9\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>9<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading3\"><h3 id=\"Relationship_between_SEO_and_large_language_models\">Relationship between SEO and large language models</h3></div>\n<p>In the 2020s, the rise of generative AI tools such as <a href=\"/wiki/ChatGPT\" title=\"ChatGPT\">ChatGPT</a>, <a href=\"/wiki/Claude_(language_model)\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Claude (language model)\">Claude</a>, <a href=\"/wiki/Perplexity_AI\" title=\"Perplexity AI\">Perplexity</a>, and <a href=\"/wiki/Gemini_(language_model)\" title=\"Gemini (language model)\">Gemini</a> began to alter how users find information online, with AI-generated answers increasingly displacing traditional search results.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-Chen2025&#95;10-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-Chen2025-10\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>10<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> In response, digital marketers developed new optimization approaches for LLM-based search, referred to as answer engine optimization (AEO) or<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-11\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-11\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>11<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> <a href=\"/wiki/Generative_engine_optimization\" title=\"Generative engine optimization\">generative engine optimization</a> (GEO).<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-Aggarwal2024&#95;12-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-Aggarwal2024-12\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>12<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> These terms are often used interchangeably,<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-13\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-13\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>13<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-14\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-14\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>14<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> and other related terms exist, such as AI engine optimization (AIEO).<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-15\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-15\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>15<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Digital marketers optimizing for GEO tend to focus on content structure, authority signals, and structured data, with the goal of becoming a trusted, citable source in AI-generated responses.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-16\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-16\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>16<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-Aggarwal2024&#95;12-1\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-Aggarwal2024-12\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>12<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-Chen2025&#95;10-1\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-Chen2025-10\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>10<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading2\"><h2 id=\"Relationship_between_Google_and_SEO_industry\">Relationship between Google and SEO industry</h2></div>\n<p>In 1998, two graduate students at <a href=\"/wiki/Stanford_University\" title=\"Stanford University\">Stanford University</a>, <a href=\"/wiki/Larry_Page\" title=\"Larry Page\">Larry Page</a> and <a href=\"/wiki/Sergey_Brin\" title=\"Sergey Brin\">Sergey Brin</a>, developed \"Backrub\", a search engine that relied on a mathematical algorithm to rate the prominence of web pages. The number calculated by the algorithm, <a href=\"/wiki/PageRank\" title=\"PageRank\">PageRank</a>, is a function of the quantity and strength of <a href=\"/wiki/Inbound_link\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Inbound link\">inbound links</a>.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-lgscalehyptxt&#95;17-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-lgscalehyptxt-17\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>17<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> PageRank estimates the likelihood that a given page will be reached by a web user who randomly surfs the web and follows links from one page to another. In effect, this means that some links are stronger than others, as a higher PageRank page is more likely to be reached by the random web surfer.\n</p><p>Page and Brin founded Google in 1998.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-18\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-18\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>18<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> Google attracted a loyal following among the growing number of <a href=\"/wiki/Internet\" title=\"Internet\">Internet</a> users, who liked its simple design.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-bbc-1&#95;19-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-bbc-1-19\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>19<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> Off-page factors (such as PageRank and hyperlink analysis) were considered as well as on-page factors (such as keyword frequency, <a href=\"/wiki/Meta_tags\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Meta tags\">meta tags</a>, headings, links and site structure) to enable Google to avoid the kind of manipulation seen in search engines that only considered on-page factors for their rankings. Although PageRank was more difficult to <a href=\"/wiki/Gaming_the_system\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Gaming the system\">game</a>, webmasters had already developed link-building tools and schemes to influence the <a href=\"/wiki/Inktomi\" title=\"Inktomi\">Inktomi</a> search engine, and these methods proved similarly applicable to gaming PageRank. Many sites focus on exchanging, buying, and selling links, often on a massive scale. Some of these schemes involved the creation of thousands of sites for the sole purpose of <a href=\"/wiki/Spamdexing\" title=\"Spamdexing\">link spamming</a>.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-20\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-20\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>20<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>By 2004, search engines had incorporated a wide range of undisclosed factors in their ranking algorithms to reduce the impact of link manipulation.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-nyt0607&#95;21-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-nyt0607-21\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>21<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> The leading search engines, Google, <a href=\"/wiki/Bing_(search_engine)\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Bing (search engine)\">Bing</a>, and <a href=\"/wiki/Yahoo\" title=\"Yahoo\">Yahoo</a>, do not disclose the algorithms they use to rank pages. Some SEO practitioners have studied different approaches to search engine optimization and have shared their personal opinions.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-22\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-22\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>22<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> Patents related to search engines can provide information to better understand search engines.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-23\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-23\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>23<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> In 2005, Google began personalizing search results for each user. Depending on their history of previous searches, Google crafted results for logged in users.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-24\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-24\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>24<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In 2007, Google announced a campaign against paid links that transfer <a href=\"/wiki/PageRank\" title=\"PageRank\">PageRank</a>.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-25\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-25\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>25<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> On June 15, 2009, Google disclosed that they had taken measures to mitigate the effects of PageRank sculpting by use of the <a href=\"/wiki/Nofollow\" title=\"Nofollow\">nofollow</a> attribute on links. <a href=\"/wiki/Matt_Cutts\" title=\"Matt Cutts\">Matt Cutts</a>, a well-known software engineer at Google, announced that Google Bot would no longer treat any no follow links, in the same way, to prevent SEO service providers from using no follow for PageRank sculpting.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-26\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-26\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>26<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> As a result of this change, the usage of no follow led to evaporation of PageRank. In order to avoid the above, SEO engineers developed alternative techniques that replace no followed tags with obfuscated <a href=\"/wiki/JavaScript\" title=\"JavaScript\">JavaScript</a> and thus permit PageRank sculpting. Additionally, several solutions have been suggested that include the usage of <a href=\"/wiki/HTML_element#Frames\" title=\"HTML element\">iframes</a>, <a href=\"/wiki/Flash_animation\" title=\"Flash animation\">Flash</a>, and JavaScript.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-27\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-27\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>27<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> As a response, in 2019, Google would change its position and started using these tags as hints as a way to better understand how to appropriately analyze and use links within their systems\".<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-28\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-28\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>28<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In December 2009, Google announced it would be using the web search history of all its users in order to populate search results.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-29\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-29\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>29<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> On June 8, 2010 a new web indexing system called <a href=\"/wiki/Google_Caffeine\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Google Caffeine\">Google Caffeine</a> was announced. Designed to allow users to find news results, forum posts, and other content much sooner after publishing than before, Google Caffeine was a change to the way Google updated its index in order to make things show up quicker on Google than before. According to Carrie Grimes, the software engineer who announced Caffeine for Google, \"Caffeine provides 50 percent fresher results for web searches than our last index...\"<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-30\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-30\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>30<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> <a href=\"/wiki/Google_Instant\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Google Instant\">Google Instant</a>, a real-time search feature, was introduced in late 2010 to deliver more timely and relevant results. Historically, site administrators often spent months or years optimizing websites to improve their search rankings. With the rise of social media platforms and blogs, major search engines adjusted their algorithms to enable fresh content to rank more quickly in search results.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-31\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-31\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>31<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Google has implemented numerous algorithm updates to improve search quality, including <a href=\"/wiki/Google_Panda\" title=\"Google Panda\">Panda (2011)</a> for content quality, <a href=\"/wiki/Google_Penguin\" title=\"Google Penguin\">Penguin (2012)</a> for link spam, <a href=\"/wiki/Google_Hummingbird\" title=\"Google Hummingbird\">Hummingbird (2013)</a> for natural language processing, and <a rel=\"nofollow\" class=\"external text\" href=\"https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/search-language-understanding-bert/\">BERT (2019)</a> for query understanding. These updates reflect the ongoing evolution of search technology and Google's efforts to combat spam while improving user experience.\n</p><p>On May 20, 2025, Google announced that AI Mode would be released to all US users. AI Mode uses what Google calls a \"query fan-out technique\" which breaks down the search query into multiple sub-topics which generates additional search queries for the user.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-32\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-32\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>32<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading2\"><h2 id=\"Methods\">Methods</h2></div>\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading3\"><h3 id=\"Getting_indexed\">Getting indexed</h3></div>\n<figure class=\"mw-default-size\" typeof=\"mw:File/Thumb\"><a href=\"/wiki/File:PageRanks-Example.svg\" class=\"mw-file-description\"><img src=\"//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/PageRanks-Example.svg/250px-PageRanks-Example.svg.png\" decoding=\"async\" width=\"250\" height=\"202\" class=\"mw-file-element\" srcset=\"//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/PageRanks-Example.svg/500px-PageRanks-Example.svg.png 2x\" data-file-width=\"758\" data-file-height=\"611\" /></a><figcaption>A simple illustration of the <a href=\"/wiki/PageRank\" title=\"PageRank\">Pagerank</a> algorithm. Percentage shows the perceived importance.</figcaption></figure>\n<p>The leading search engines, such as Google, Bing and Yahoo!, use <a href=\"/wiki/Web_crawler\" title=\"Web crawler\">crawlers</a> to find pages for their algorithmic search results. Pages that are linked from other search engine-indexed pages do not need to be submitted because they are found automatically. The <a href=\"/wiki/Yahoo!_Directory\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Yahoo! Directory\">Yahoo! Directory</a> and <a href=\"/wiki/DMOZ\" title=\"DMOZ\">DMOZ</a>, two major directories which closed in 2014 and 2017 respectively, both required manual submission and human editorial review.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-33\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-33\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>33<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> Google offers <a href=\"/wiki/Google_Webmaster_Tools\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Google Webmaster Tools\">Google Search Console</a>, for which an XML <a href=\"/wiki/Sitemap\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Sitemap\">Sitemap</a> feed can be created and submitted for free to ensure that all pages are found, especially pages that are not discoverable by automatically following links<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-34\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-34\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>34<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> in addition to their URL submission console.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-35\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-35\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>35<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> Yahoo! formerly operated a paid submission service that guaranteed to crawl for a <a href=\"/wiki/Pay_per_click\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Pay per click\">cost per click</a>;<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-36\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-36\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>36<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> however, this practice was discontinued in 2009. Nevertheless, SEO tools such as <a href=\"/wiki/Semrush\" title=\"Semrush\">Semrush</a> enable analysis of both paid and organic traffic by providing insights into cost per click and keyword performance.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-37\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-37\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>37<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p><a href=\"/wiki/Web_search_engine\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Web search engine\">Search engine</a> crawlers may look at a number of different factors when <a href=\"/wiki/Web_crawler\" title=\"Web crawler\">crawling</a> a site. Not every page is indexed by search engines. The distance of pages from the root directory of a site may also be a factor in whether or not pages get crawled.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-cho&#95;38-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-cho-38\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>38<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Mobile devices are used for the majority of Google searches.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-39\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-39\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>39<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> In November 2016, Google announced a major change to the way they are crawling websites and started to make their index mobile-first, which means the mobile version of a given website becomes the starting point for what Google includes in their index.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-40\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-40\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>40<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading3\"><h3 id=\"Preventing_crawling\">Preventing crawling</h3></div>\n<link rel=\"mw-deduplicated-inline-style\" href=\"mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1353705441\" /><div role=\"note\" class=\"hatnote navigation-not-searchable\">Main article: <a href=\"/wiki/Robots_exclusion_standard\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Robots exclusion standard\">Robots exclusion standard</a></div>\n<p>To avoid undesirable content in the search indexes, webmasters can instruct spiders not to crawl certain files or directories through the standard <a href=\"/wiki/Robots.txt\" title=\"Robots.txt\">robots.txt</a> file in the root directory of the domain. Additionally, a page can be explicitly excluded from a search engine's database by using a <a href=\"/wiki/Meta_tag\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Meta tag\">meta tag</a> specific to robots (usually &lt;meta name=\"robots\" content=\"noindex\"&gt; ). When a search engine visits a site, the robots.txt located in the <a href=\"/wiki/Root_directory\" title=\"Root directory\">root directory</a> is the first file crawled. The robots.txt file is then parsed and will instruct the robot as to which pages are not to be crawled. As a search engine crawler may keep a cached copy of this file, it may on occasion crawl pages a webmaster does not wish to crawl. Pages typically prevented from being crawled include login-specific pages such as shopping carts and user-specific content such as search results from internal searches. In March 2007, Google warned webmasters that they should prevent indexing of internal search results because those pages are considered search spam.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-41\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-41\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>41<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p><p>In 2020, Google <a href=\"/wiki/Sunset_provision\" title=\"Sunset provision\">sunsetted</a> the standard (and open-sourced their code) and now treats it as a hint rather than a directive. To adequately ensure that pages are not indexed, a page-level robot's meta tag should be included.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-42\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-42\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>42<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading3\"><h3 id=\"Increasing_prominence\">Increasing prominence</h3></div>\n<p>A variety of methods can increase the prominence of a webpage within the search results. <a href=\"/wiki/Methods_of_website_linking\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Methods of website linking\">Cross linking</a> between pages of the same website to provide more links to important pages may improve its visibility. Page design makes users trust a site and want to stay once they find it. When people bounce off a site, it counts against the site and affects its credibility.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-:0&#95;43-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-:0-43\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>43<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p><p>Writing content that includes frequently searched keyword phrases so as to be relevant to a wide variety of search queries will tend to increase traffic. Updating content so as to keep search engines crawling back frequently can give additional weight to a site. Adding relevant keywords to a web page's metadata, including the <a href=\"/wiki/HEAD_tag\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"HEAD tag\">title tag and meta description</a>, will tend to improve the relevancy of a site's search listings, thus increasing traffic. <a href=\"/wiki/URL_canonicalization\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"URL canonicalization\">URL canonicalization</a> of web pages accessible via multiple URLs, using the <a href=\"/wiki/Canonical_link_element\" title=\"Canonical link element\">canonical link element</a><sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-44\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-44\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>44<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> or via <a href=\"/wiki/301_redirect\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"301 redirect\">301 redirects</a> can help make sure links to different versions of the URL all count towards the page's link popularity score. These are known as incoming links, which point to the URL and can count towards the page link's popularity score, impacting the credibility of a website.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-:0&#95;43-1\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-:0-43\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>43<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p>\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading3\"><h3 id=\"White_hat_versus_black_hat_techniques\">White hat versus black hat techniques</h3></div>\n<link rel=\"mw-deduplicated-inline-style\" href=\"mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1360160623\" /><table class=\"box-Update plainlinks metadata ambox ambox-content ambox-Update\" role=\"presentation\"><tbody><tr><td class=\"mbox-image\"><div class=\"mbox-image-div\"><span typeof=\"mw:File\"><span><img alt=\"\" src=\"//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Ambox_current_red_Americas.svg/60px-Ambox_current_red_Americas.svg.png\" decoding=\"async\" width=\"42\" height=\"34\" class=\"mw-file-element\" srcset=\"//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/53/Ambox_current_red_Americas.svg/120px-Ambox_current_red_Americas.svg.png 2x\" data-file-width=\"360\" data-file-height=\"290\" /></span></span></div></td><td class=\"mbox-text\"><div class=\"mbox-text-span\">This section needs to be <b>updated</b>.<span class=\"hide-when-compact\"> Please help update this article to reflect recent events or newly available information.</span>  <span class=\"date-container\"><i>(<span class=\"date\">September 2025</span>)</i></span></div></td></tr></tbody></table>\n<figure typeof=\"mw:File/Thumb\"><a href=\"/wiki/File:Demystifying_Search_Engine_Optimization_-viz_notes-_-wcyvr_(8084222814).jpg\" class=\"mw-file-description\"><img src=\"//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/Demystifying_Search_Engine_Optimization_-viz_notes-_-wcyvr_%288084222814%29.jpg/500px-Demystifying_Search_Engine_Optimization_-viz_notes-_-wcyvr_%288084222814%29.jpg\" decoding=\"async\" width=\"400\" height=\"300\" class=\"mw-file-element\" srcset=\"//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/Demystifying_Search_Engine_Optimization_-viz_notes-_-wcyvr_%288084222814%29.jpg/960px-Demystifying_Search_Engine_Optimization_-viz_notes-_-wcyvr_%288084222814%29.jpg 2x\" data-file-width=\"1024\" data-file-height=\"768\" /></a><figcaption>Common white-hat methods of search engine optimization</figcaption></figure>\n<p>SEO techniques are often classified into two broad categories: techniques that search engine companies recommend (\"white hat\"),<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-45\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-45\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>45<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> and those techniques of which search engines do not approve (\"black hat\"). \n</p><p>Search engines attempt to minimize the effect of the latter, among them <a href=\"/wiki/Spamdexing\" title=\"Spamdexing\">spamdexing</a>. Industry commentators have classified these methods and the practitioners who employ them as either <a href=\"/wiki/White_hat_(computer_security)\" title=\"White hat (computer security)\">white hat</a> SEO or <a href=\"/wiki/Black_hat_hacking\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Black hat hacking\">black hat</a> SEO.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-46\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-46\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>46<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p><p>A white hat SEO technique conforms to the search engines' guidelines. It's been compared to web development that promotes accessibility,<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-47\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-47\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>47<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> although the two are not identical. \n</p><p>Black hat SEO attempts to improve rankings in ways that are disapproved of by the search engines or involve deception. A dated black hat technique involves using hidden text, either as text colored similar to the background, in an invisible <a href=\"/wiki/Span_and_div\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Span and div\">div</a>, or positioned off-screen. Search engines like Google have strong policies against many of these tactics<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-48\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-48\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>48<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>.\n</p><p>White hat tactics tend to produce results that last a long time, whereas black hat tactics create the risk that sites may eventually be punished once the search engines discover what they are doing.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-49\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-49\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>49<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>Another method gives a different page depending on whether the page is being requested by a human visitor or a search engine, a technique known as <a href=\"/wiki/Cloaking\" title=\"Cloaking\">cloaking</a>.<sup class=\"noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact\" style=\"white-space:nowrap;\">&#91;<i><a href=\"/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed\" title=\"Wikipedia:Citation needed\"><span title=\"This claim needs references to reliable sources. (June 2026)\">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>\n</p><p>Another category sometimes used is <a href=\"/wiki/Grey_hat\" title=\"Grey hat\">grey hat SEO</a>. This is in between the black hat and white hat approaches, where the methods employed avoid the site being penalized but do not act in producing the best content for users.<sup class=\"noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact\" style=\"white-space:nowrap;\">&#91;<i><a href=\"/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed\" title=\"Wikipedia:Citation needed\"><span title=\"This claim needs references to reliable sources. (June 2026)\">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup>\n</p><p>Search engines may penalize sites they discover using black or grey hat methods, either by reducing their rankings or eliminating their listings from their databases altogether. Such penalties can be applied either automatically by the search engines' algorithms or by a manual site review. One example was the February 2006 Google removal of both <a href=\"/wiki/BMW\" title=\"BMW\">BMW</a> Germany and <a href=\"/wiki/Ricoh\" title=\"Ricoh\">Ricoh</a> Germany for the use of deceptive practices.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-intwebspam&#95;50-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-intwebspam-50\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>50<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> Both companies subsequently apologized, fixed the offending pages, and were restored to Google's search engine results page.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-51\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-51\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>51<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Companies that employ black hat techniques or other spammy tactics can get their client websites banned from the search results. In 2005, the <i><a href=\"/wiki/Wall_Street_Journal\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Wall Street Journal\">Wall Street Journal</a></i> reported on a company, <a href=\"/wiki/Traffic_Power\" title=\"Traffic Power\">Traffic Power</a>, which allegedly used high-risk techniques and failed to disclose those risks to its clients.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-52\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-52\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>52<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> <i><a href=\"/wiki/Wired_(magazine)\" title=\"Wired (magazine)\">Wired</a></i> magazine reported that the same company sued blogger and SEO Aaron Wall for writing about the ban.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-wired09082005&#95;53-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-wired09082005-53\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>53<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> Google's <a href=\"/wiki/Matt_Cutts\" title=\"Matt Cutts\">Matt Cutts</a> later confirmed that Google had banned Traffic Power and some of its clients.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-54\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-54\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>54<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading2\"><h2 id=\"As_marketing_strategy\">As marketing strategy</h2></div>\n<p>SEO is one approach within digital marketing, alongside other strategies such as pay-per-click advertising and social media marketing. <a href=\"/wiki/Search_engine_marketing\" title=\"Search engine marketing\">Search engine marketing (SEM)</a> is the practice of designing, running, and optimizing search engine ad campaigns. Its difference from SEO is most simply depicted as the difference between paid and unpaid priority ranking in search results. SEM focuses on prominence more so than relevance; website developers should regard SEM with the utmost importance with consideration to visibility as most navigate to the primary listings of their search.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-55\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-55\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>55<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> A successful Internet marketing campaign may also depend upon building high-quality web pages to engage and persuade internet users, setting up <a href=\"/wiki/Web_analytics\" title=\"Web analytics\">analytics</a> programs to enable site owners to measure results, and improving a site's <a href=\"/wiki/Conversion_rate\" class=\"mw-redirect\" title=\"Conversion rate\">conversion rate</a>.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-56\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-56\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>56<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-57\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-57\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>57<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p><p>In November 2015, Google released a full 160-page version of its Search Quality Rating Guidelines to the public,<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-58\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-58\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>58<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> which revealed a shift in their focus towards \"usefulness\" and <a href=\"/wiki/Mobile_local_search\" title=\"Mobile local search\">mobile local search</a>. In recent years the mobile market has exploded, overtaking the use of desktops, as shown in by <a href=\"/wiki/StatCounter\" title=\"StatCounter\">StatCounter</a> in October 2016, where they analyzed 2.5 million websites and found that 51.3% of the pages were loaded by a mobile device.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-59\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-59\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>59<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> Google has been one of the companies that are utilizing the popularity of mobile usage by encouraging websites to use their <a href=\"/wiki/Google_Search_Console\" title=\"Google Search Console\">Google Search Console</a>, the Mobile-Friendly Test, which allows companies to measure up their website to the search engine results and determine how user-friendly their websites are. The closer the keywords are together their ranking will improve based on key terms.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-:0&#95;43-2\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-:0-43\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>43<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>SEO may generate an adequate <a href=\"/wiki/Return_on_investment\" title=\"Return on investment\">return on investment</a>. However, search engines are not paid for organic search traffic, their algorithms change, and there are no guarantees of continued referrals. Due to this lack of guarantee and uncertainty, a business that relies heavily on search engine traffic can suffer major losses if the search engines stop sending visitors.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-60\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-60\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>60<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> Search engines can change their algorithms, impacting a website's search engine ranking, possibly resulting in a serious loss of traffic. According to Google's CEO, <a href=\"/wiki/Eric_Schmidt\" title=\"Eric Schmidt\">Eric Schmidt</a>, in 2010, Google made over 500 algorithm changes \u2013 almost 1.5 per day.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-61\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-61\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>61<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> Industry analysts note that websites may face risks from algorithm changes that can significantly impact organic traffic. In addition to accessibility in terms of web crawlers (addressed above), user <a href=\"/wiki/Web_accessibility\" title=\"Web accessibility\">web accessibility</a> has become increasingly important for SEO.\n</p>\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading2\"><h2 id=\"International_markets_and_SEO\">International markets and SEO</h2></div>\n<p>Optimization techniques are highly tuned to the dominant search engines in the target market. The search engines' market shares vary from market to market, as does competition. Google has maintained dominant market share in most regions, with varying percentages by market.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-62\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-62\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>62<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> In markets outside the United States, Google's share is often larger, and data showed Google was the dominant search engine worldwide as of 2007.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-63\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-63\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>63<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> As of 2006, Google had an 85\u201390% market share in Germany.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-grehan-1&#95;64-0\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-grehan-1-64\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>64<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> As of March 2024, Google still had a significant market share of 89.85% in Germany.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-65\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-65\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>65<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> As of March 2024, Google's market share in the UK was 93.61%.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-66\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-66\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>66<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>Successful search engine optimization (SEO) for international markets requires more than just translating web pages. It may also involve registering a domain name with a <a href=\"/wiki/Country_code_top-level_domain\" title=\"Country code top-level domain\">country-code top-level domain</a> (ccTLD) or a relevant <a href=\"/wiki/Top-level_domain\" title=\"Top-level domain\">top-level domain</a> (TLD) for the target market, choosing web hosting with a local IP address or server, and using a <a href=\"/wiki/Content_delivery_network\" title=\"Content delivery network\">Content Delivery Network</a> (CDN) to improve website speed and performance globally.  It is also important to understand the local culture so that the content feels relevant to the audience. This includes conducting keyword research for each market, using hreflang tags to target the right languages, and building local backlinks. However, the core SEO principles\u2014such as creating high-quality content, improving user experience, and building links\u2014remain the same, regardless of language or region.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-grehan-1&#95;64-1\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-grehan-1-64\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>64<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> \n</p><p>Regional search engines have a strong presence in specific markets:\n</p>\n<ul><li>China: <a href=\"/wiki/Baidu\" title=\"Baidu\">Baidu</a> leads the market, controlling about 70 to 80% market share.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-67\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-67\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>67<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>South Korea: Since the end of 2021, <a href=\"/wiki/Naver\" title=\"Naver\">Naver</a>, a domestic web portal, has gained prominence in the country.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-68\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-68\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>68<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-69\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-69\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>69<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup></li>\n<li>Russia: <a href=\"/wiki/Yandex\" title=\"Yandex\">Yandex</a> is the leading search engine in Russia. As of December 2023, it accounted for at least 63.8% of the market share.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-70\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-70\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>70<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup></li></ul>\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading3\"><h3 id=\"Multilingual_SEO\">Multilingual SEO</h3></div>\n<p>By the early 2000s, businesses recognized that the web and search engines could help them reach global audiences. As a result, the need for multilingual SEO emerged.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-71\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-71\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>71<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup> In the early years of international SEO development, simple translation was seen as sufficient. However, over time, it became clear that localization and transcreation\u2014adapting content to local language, culture, and emotional resonance\u2014were more effective than basic translation.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-72\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-72\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>72<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading2\"><h2 id=\"Legal_cases\">Legal cases</h2></div>\n<p>On October 17, 2002, SearchKing filed suit in the <a href=\"/wiki/United_States_district_court\" title=\"United States district court\">United States District Court</a>, Western District of Oklahoma, against the search engine Google. SearchKing's claim was that Google's tactics to prevent spamdexing constituted a <a href=\"/wiki/Tortious_interference\" title=\"Tortious interference\">tortious interference</a> with contractual relations.  On May 27, 2003, the court granted Google's motion to dismiss the complaint because SearchKing \"failed to state a claim upon which relief may be granted.\"<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-73\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-73\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>73<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-74\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-74\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>74<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p><p>In March 2006, KinderStart filed a lawsuit against Google over search engine rankings. KinderStart's website was removed from Google's index prior to the lawsuit, and the amount of traffic to the site dropped by 70%. On March 16, 2007, the <a href=\"/wiki/United_States_District_Court_for_the_Northern_District_of_California\" title=\"United States District Court for the Northern District of California\">United States District Court for the Northern District of California</a> (<a href=\"/wiki/San_Jose,_California\" title=\"San Jose, California\">San Jose</a> Division) dismissed KinderStart's complaint without leave to amend and partially granted Google's motion for <a href=\"/wiki/Federal_Rules_of_Civil_Procedure#Title_III_.E2.80.93_Pleadings_and_Motions\" title=\"Federal Rules of Civil Procedure\">Rule 11</a> sanctions against KinderStart's attorney, requiring him to pay part of Google's legal expenses.<sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-75\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-75\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>75<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup><sup id=\"cite&#95;ref-76\" class=\"reference\"><a href=\"#cite_note-76\"><span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#91;</span>76<span class=\"cite-bracket\">&#93;</span></a></sup>\n</p>\n<div class=\"mw-heading mw-heading2\"><h2 id=\"See_also\">See also</h2></div>\n<style
